adjudications.signal: Velmere local heuristic: Unchecked low-level call result in aggregate
adjudications.rationale: The exact deployed source stores call success in `success` and immediately executes `require(success, "Multicall3: call failed")`. Slither reports the low-level call only as informational and Aderyn does not report an unchecked-low-level-call issue.

adjudications.signal: Slither arbitrary-send-eth + Aderyn ETH transferred without address checks in aggregate3Value
adjudications.rationale: Arbitrary target/value forwarding is an intended multicall capability and alone is not unauthorized transfer. Both independent tools correctly highlight the high-risk value-sending surface. The customer-relevant issue is the separately reproduced failure-tolerant retained-value behavior.

adjudications.signal: Aderyn Loop Contains require/revert + Slither calls-loop
adjudications.rationale: Functions intentionally provide strict and failure-tolerant variants. A strict call reverting the batch when failure is disallowed matches the documented API contract. This remains a gas/availability design consideration, not an independently demonstrated vulnerability.

adjudications.signal: Aderyn Public Function Not Used Internally
adjudications.rationale: Visibility can potentially be external for gas/interface hygiene but no security impact is demonstrated.

confirmedFindings.title: Value remains in Multicall3 when a value-bearing allowed subcall fails
confirmedFindings.description: When a Call3Value item has nonzero `value`, `allowFailure=true`, and the target subcall reverts, the EVM reverts the subcall value transfer but Multicall3 intentionally allows the outer batch to continue. Because final validation only checks `msg.value == sum(call.value)` and the ABI exposes no explicit withdraw/sweep/recover function, the failed call's value remains on Multicall3 instead of returning to the caller.
confirmedFindings.impact: A caller can lose access to the ETH allocated to a failure-tolerant subcall if that subcall fails. No attacker theft, privilege escalation, or unauthorized third-party transfer path has been established.
confirmedFindings.likelihoodBoundary: Requires the caller/integrator to combine nonzero value with `allowFailure=true` and the target call to fail. Production frequency is not established.
confirmedFindings.currentDeploymentBalanceContext: A non-zero deployed balance was observed, but the evidence does not attribute that balance to this exact failure path; forced ETH or other causes remain possible.

externalCorrelation.aderyn: ETH transferred without address checks on aggregate3Value
externalCorrelation.note: External analyzers identify the value-sending surface; behavioral reproduction proves the retained-value failure mode.

remediation.candidate: Reject `allowFailure=true` when the corresponding call has nonzero value, or explicitly refund failed-call value to the caller.

truthBoundary: This is an AI-assisted evidence consolidation and review packet, not a qualified human architecture/security sign-off. The confirmed finding is backed by exact deployed source, two independent static analyzer families, deterministic behavioral reproduction and remediation retest; final human severity/business-logic approval remains mandatory under the current Velmere A03/A05 policy.
